Done. I wrote `out/T4/solution.py`, ran it once with `python out/T4/solution.py`, and it succeeded on the first attempt, producing `out/T4/model.safetensors` with 244 tensors (64 merged). Summary:

- Verifies base/ft1/ft2 have identical tensor name sets and that all 180 non-MLP tensors are bit-exact identical across all three checkpoints — aborts loudly otherwise.
- For each of the 64 MLP tensors, computes `base + λ*(ft1-base) + λ*(ft2-base)` (λ=0.4) in float32 against the unmodified base, casts to float16.
- Copies all other tensors unchanged from base.
- Asserts exactly 64 merged tensors and exactly 244 output tensors before writing.

Also wrote `out/T4/REPORT.md` with the participant self-report.
